root.statement: Choose and implement a coherent Soltex interaction system that removes default whole-page scrolling and persistent explanatory clutter without weakening existing behavior or honest capability boundaries.
root.source_state: The pushed 1facf37 native UI is functional but repeats dark SaaS cards, violet selection fills, eyebrow-title-subtitle templates, and long explanation panels across primary workspaces.
root.target_state: Every primary workspace follows the Quiet Instrument Deck contract, presents direct controls first, and fits its common path within the 1280 by 820 reference viewport.
conditions: Preserve working controls, persistent state, lifecycle fixes, preview labels, security boundaries, and protected checkout ownership.
Do not copy proprietary code, assets, copy, presets, measurements, or distinctive layouts from reference products.
Reserve subjective visual acceptance and residual accessibility approval for the user.
root.boundary: The sol/soltex-product-rebuild worktree, its native WPF UI, tests, documentation, and generated local evidence; no production deployment or external account mutation.

intent.summary: Make Soltex feel like a deliberate native system utility with less scrolling, less visible prose, and more direct manipulation.

decision.summary: Adopt Quiet Instrument Deck and migrate the highest-friction workspaces before additional product expansion.

acceptance_contract.summary: Default primary views fit at 1280 by 820, controls precede commentary, no feature regression is accepted, and owner visual acceptance remains explicit.
acceptance_contract.unknown_disposition: Owner visual approval and final accessibility disposition remain open until post-implementation native review.

mechanism.summary: Shared theme tokens and components define the visual grammar; each workspace uses a compact command header plus a bounded table, lane, or master-detail work area.

current_state_history.summary: Baseline identity is branch sol/soltex-product-rebuild at 1facf373 with a complete current-source capture matrix dated 2026-08-12.

people_incentives.summary: The user owns subjective visual acceptance and wants a calm, capable app rather than an AI-generated dashboard aesthetic.

lifecycle_recovery.summary: Changes remain isolated in the implementation worktree; the full build, focused suites, and 16-state native candidate matrix passed, and a bounded capture timeout recovered without an orphan process or overlapping retry.
lifecycle_recovery.unknown_disposition: Signed installer recovery and broad display/accessibility recovery remain separate later gates.

invariants.statement: Existing working commands, persistence, and lifecycle behavior remain functional.
Working, preview, unavailable, and degraded capability remain visibly distinct.
Reference products contribute only general principles; no proprietary payload or distinctive expression is copied.
Subjective visual acceptance and residual accessibility approval remain reserved for the user.

dependencies.name: Soltex WPF theme resources
dependencies.role: Shared source of palette, geometry, typography, and reusable component behavior.

dependencies.name: Native render-smoke evidence
dependencies.role: Endpoint evidence for viewport, layout, and runtime integration.

stakeholders.name: Soltex owner
stakeholders.role: Objective owner and final subjective visual accepter.

authority.scope: Modify, test, document, and capture the dedicated Soltex product-rebuild worktree and push the established feature branch and draft PR.
authorized_actions: Edit in-scope WPF source, tests, documentation, and local evidence.
Run bounded local builds, tests, render smoke, and package verification.
Commit and push the established implementation branch and update its draft pull request.
forbidden_actions: Reset, clean, stash, discard, or overwrite the protected owner checkout.
Copy or redistribute proprietary reference-product payloads or distinctive expression.
Claim owner visual acceptance, WCAG conformance, feature parity, or production readiness without evidence.

hard_gates.rationale: The user explicitly authorized the full design-system rework and implementation.
The work changes UI presentation and bounded app behavior while preserving existing lifecycle and security controls.
The clean-room boundary is documented and no private data or proprietary payload is acquired.
Only reversible Git branch and draft pull-request updates are authorized external state.
No destructive operation or production deployment is in scope.
Implementation may proceed while final subjective acceptance remains explicitly reserved.
The isolated worktree and file-level Git history support bounded recovery without touching owner work.

findings.label: OBSERVED
findings.statement: Security, Updates, Remote Assist, and Settings present several equal-weight rounded cards and persistent explanations before or around the primary work.

findings.label: OBSERVED
findings.statement: Applications and default Performance already use real dense data surfaces that provide a credible system-utility foundation.

findings.label: UNKNOWN
findings.statement: The reworked visual system cannot be accepted until native after-captures are reviewed by the user.

functional_implementation.signal: Shared tokens, navigation signal, compact command shelves, local modes, and bounded work areas are implemented across every primary and preview workspace.
functional_implementation.rationale: The affected control suite passed 29 of 29 after the migration, including mutually exclusive Performance, Settings, and Audio work areas.

runtime_integration.signal: Release build and all required suites passed; 16 independent native WPF states rendered at 1280 by 820 without an error sidecar.
runtime_integration.rationale: Native execution exercised the default and disclosure paths changed by the design migration.

player_eye_presentation.signal: Agent cold-eye comparison found no gross clipping, hidden common-path command, whole-page default scroll, or obvious copy-budget breach across the 16-state candidate matrix.
player_eye_presentation.rationale: This passes the bounded reference-viewport presentation gate while leaving subjective owner acceptance separate.

evidence_regression_coverage.signal: Design-token and identity policies, Release build, eight functional suites, and the complete candidate matrix passed.
evidence_regression_coverage.rationale: The evidence covers theme policy, behavior, security boundaries, lifecycle-dependent rendering, and all changed native states.

human_acceptance.signal: No owner decision exists for the reworked UI.
human_acceptance.rationale: Subjective quality remains a human-reserved decision.

claims.label: OBSERVED
claims.statement: The current primary UI overuses whole-page scrolling, repeated card stacks, persistent explanatory text, and a violet dark-SaaS treatment that weakens a system-utility identity.

confidence.basis: The complete current-source capture matrix and current XAML independently expose the repeated layout and copy patterns.

claims.label: MEASURED
claims.statement: A shared Quiet Instrument Deck theme plus bounded command-header and work-area templates will reduce visual noise while preserving capability discoverability.

confidence.basis: The rights-safe design contract is implemented, all named regression gates passed, and the complete native candidate matrix supports the intended viewport and hierarchy outcome.

evidence.integrity: Current-source native capture set at branch head 1facf373; primary/default and disclosure states inspected before source-led interpretation.
Inspected in clean worktree at 1facf373 before rework edits.
Version 2.0 Quiet Instrument Deck implementation contract.
Dated clean-room record; all sources marked REFERENCE ONLY and no payload acquired.

evidence.locator: eng/verify-design-tokens.ps1; passed across 10 XAML files on the working candidate
evidence.integrity: Raw colour use remained confined to the shared token dictionary after the full migration.

Release build completed with zero warnings or errors; required suites passed at Security 31/31, supply chain 18/18, hardening 12/12, Updates 17/17, Device Fabric 24/24, Monitoring 16/16, Audio 21/21, and App 29/29.

Sixteen 1280 by 820 working-candidate native states were directly inspected. The first bounded batch ended after 13 frames with no process remaining; the final three states were captured once in a separate bounded continuation.

hypotheses.statement: Replacing page-level scroll and card stacks with a command header plus bounded work area will make the common path faster to parse without hiding advanced capability.
hypotheses.mechanism: Stable spatial regions preserve control location while local tabs and master-detail panes defer uncommon detail without removing it.
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: At 1280 by 820 every primary default view will expose its main control or data surface without whole-page scrolling and with no more than 75 explanatory words.
hypotheses.falsifier: A primary common-path action is hidden, requires additional navigation, or the default page still needs whole-page scrolling at the reference viewport.
hypotheses.decision_if_true: Retain the workbench grammar and migrate remaining preview/detail states consistently.

confidence.basis: The complete candidate matrix and affected control tests support the predicted reference-viewport result without a common-path regression.

tests.question: Which current Soltex regions create the strongest hierarchy, scrolling, copy, and interaction friction before source interpretation?

predicted_outcomes.outcome: Repeated card/prose stacks and whole-page scrolling concentrate in Security, Updates, Remote Assist, Settings, and expanded Performance detail.

tests.changes_decision_if: If direct-control surfaces were already dominant across all primary views, a theme-only correction would be sufficient.

tests.question: Does the implemented design meet viewport, interaction, accessibility, and regression boundaries in the native WPF runtime?

predicted_outcomes.outcome: Primary default workspaces expose the common path without whole-page scrolling, retain advanced detail locally, and pass affected regression suites.

tests.changes_decision_if: Any hidden primary action, clipping, focus failure, copy-budget breach, or behavioral regression requires another implementation iteration.

bounds.stop_rule: Expand only branches that change workspace anatomy, capability discoverability, regression risk, clean-room compliance, or the human acceptance gate.

nodes.statement: Select a coherent system-wide design response to the observed UI friction.
Equal-weight panels, repeated prose, and page scrolling fragment attention and make capability feel less direct.
Shared tokens and bounded workspace templates move primary controls into stable visible regions while retaining detail locally.

edges.source_delta: Primary views repeat page-level scrolling, equally emphasized cards, and explanatory text.
edges.mechanism: Competing regions dilute visual priority and force spatial context switches before the user reaches the main control.
conditions: Primary action is below or surrounded by explanation
edges.lag: Immediate during visual parsing and navigation.
edges.target_delta: The common path takes more scanning and scrolling to locate.

detection.signal: Native capture shows page scrollbars, repeated peer cards, and persistent explanatory blocks.
detection.latency: Visible in the first cold-eye pass.
detection.failure_to_detect: A cropped screenshot could omit off-screen content; the full state matrix and XAML provide a cross-check.

edges.falsifier: All primary common-path controls are immediately visible and unambiguous without page scrolling.

confidence.basis: Supported by current native captures and current source.

edges.source_delta: The design contract limits visible prose and peer regions while requiring a stable command header and work area.
edges.mechanism: Stable position and progressive disclosure reduce competing targets while preserving advanced capability in local panes.
edges.lag: After the system-wide XAML migration and native revalidation.
edges.target_delta: Primary work becomes visible and spatially predictable with less scrolling and less prose.

detection.signal: After-capture matrix, word/scroll audit, keyboard checks, and affected tests.
detection.latency: At each atomic workspace migration and final native matrix.
detection.failure_to_detect: Screenshots alone cannot reveal keyboard, scaling, lifecycle, or owner preference failures.

edges.falsifier: Any common-path control becomes harder to find, page scrolling remains, or behavioral/accessibility regression appears.

confidence.basis: The mechanism is plausible and rights-safe but needs final runtime and human evidence.

thresholds.boundary: No more than 75 visible words outside live data, labels, errors, and accessible names.
Zero whole-page vertical scrolling at 1280 by 820; bounded work regions may scroll internally.
thresholds.direction: Revise when a common-path page requires scrolling.

decision.recommendation: Freeze the implemented Quiet Instrument Deck candidate, bind an exact-commit native matrix, and ask the owner for a KEEP, REVISE, or REJECT decision while keyboard, scaling, high-contrast, and UI Automation gates continue separately.
rejected_options: A palette-only reskin would preserve the same information architecture and scrolling failure.
Copying a reference product one-to-one would violate the clean-room boundary and Soltex identity.
Adding sliders decoratively would misrepresent discrete or read-only state.
decision.reopen_trigger: Reopen the design direction if native evidence shows hidden common-path controls, unresolved whole-page scrolling, accessibility regression, or owner rejection.

actions.description: Apply the Quiet Instrument Deck token, component, copy, and workspace anatomy contract across all primary Soltex views, then run native and behavioral verification.
actions.authority_basis: The user explicitly requested a total UI rework, design system, reference study, implementation, and structured remaining-work map.
actions.monitoring: The diff, design guard, full required suites, and all 16 reference-viewport states were reviewed; exact-commit capture and owner acceptance remain the next gates.

rollback.procedure: Use bounded file-level inverse patches or a new corrective commit on the isolated branch; never reset or clean the owner checkout.
preconditions: Identify exact task-owned files and current branch identity
rollback.verification: Confirm expected Git diff, rebuild, rerun affected tests, and recapture corrected native states.
rollback.irreversible_residue: Published Git history remains if a pushed commit is later corrected.

recovery.procedure: Restore the last verified theme/workspace state using a bounded corrective commit and relaunch the native capture harness.

mechanism.signal: Shared theme primitives and workspace templates compiled and passed affected control tests across every migrated surface.
mechanism.rationale: The intended bounded-workbench mechanism is present and behaviorally exercised.

endpoint.signal: All 16 working-candidate states rendered and passed agent cold-eye inspection at the 1280 by 820 reference viewport.
endpoint.rationale: The bounded endpoint passes agent inspection; human acceptance remains explicitly separate and unknown.

guardrails.signal: Clean-room provenance, token policy, functional suites, capability labels, and reference-viewport bounds passed.
guardrails.rationale: Exercised guardrails pass; broader scaling, assistive-technology, and owner gates remain named residual work rather than silently inferred.

recovery.signal: A bounded capture batch timeout left no owned process and resumed only the three missing states; build and lifecycle-dependent shutdown tests remained green.
recovery.rationale: The observed failure was retained and recovered without overlapping work or discarding source.

closure.summary: Quiet Instrument Deck is implemented and passes the bounded working-candidate build, regression, policy, and 16-state native gate; exact-commit binding and owner visual/accessibility acceptance remain open.
residual_risks: WPF scaling and high-contrast behavior may expose layout or token defects not visible at the reference viewport.
Keyboard focus restoration and UI Automation quality require dedicated evidence.
Owner visual preference cannot be inferred from automated evidence.
nonclaims: This ledger records auditable claims and decisions, not hidden chain-of-thought.
The design contract does not itself prove implementation quality or runtime correctness.
Native screenshots and green tests will not by themselves grant owner visual acceptance or WCAG conformance.
